newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Spicers sees reduced year profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Spicers sees reduced year profit.

text.p: Spicers Paper Ltd said on Friday that it now forecast a reduced profit for the year to June 30 due to a continuation of the fall in domestic paper prices.

However, the paper merchant and distributor said it expected the recent recovery in overseas prices, in Europe and in particular in the United States, to filter through to its markets in coming months.
Managing director Peter Hammond said paper prices had been expected to remain at their previous subdued level, but had in fact declined further.
"As a result, although profit for the six months to June will be better than for the same period last year, it will be down on forecast," Hammond said in a statement.
Spicers, which is 42 percent owned by Amcor Ltd, had forecast a second half net profit of about A$7 million, compared with A$2 million in the previous corresponding period.
Analysts said the profit warning indicated full year profit would come in below current expectations of about A$12 million, compared with about A$16 million in 1995/96.
Hammond said underlying demand remained strong.
Spicers had retained or increased market share and sales to major markets were above expectations. The company also expected to benefit from cost reduction programmes already in place.
